newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turkish Koc exceeds growth target in Q1.
newsitem.headline: Turkish Koc exceeds growth target in Q1.

text.p: The turnover of Turkish industrial conglomerate Koc Group grew by about 19 percent in the first quarter of 1997 in real terms, exceeding the company's 13-14 percent annual growth target, a senior company official said.

"We have a 13-14 percent growth rate target in 1997, but the results of the first three months showed that we exceeded this target by approximately six points," Necati Arikan, strategic planning president of Koc Holding, told Reuters in an interview.
He said the growth rate might not remain as rapid for the rest of the year because the markets were generally more active in the early months of the year.
"We grew faster in white goods, in the finance sectors and motor vehicle production arm Otosan where our market shares continued to expand," Arikan added.
He said the growth rate was 75 percent in the finance sector and more than 60 percent in the Otosan group, a Koc Holding and Ford Motor Co venture which produces cars and commercial vehicles.
"In the first quarter, our market share in the domestic white goods market expanded to 56 percent from 55 percent in the first three months of 1996," Arikan said.
The group's durables producers are Arcelik, Beko and Ardem.
The conglomerate increased overall exports by 11 percent to $981 million in 1996 from $884 million in 1995, but expects exports to reach around $800 million this year.

Arikan said the downturn in 1997 exports would be temporary, "Because passenger car exports by (leading car producer) Tofas will fall sharply this year as a result of the delay in new model investments in 1996 which was caused by uncertainty in the government's approach to this sector."
Tofas, which produces Fiat cars for the domestic market, is a joint venture of Koc Holding and Italian Fiat SpA. Each partner has a 37.86 percent stake in the company.
Tofas plans to spend $262 million this year on production lines for new models Palio, Siena, Marea and Bravo and hopes to begin exporting them next year. Tofas's exports were $275 million in 1996.

Koc group's overall investments will be around $700 million in 1997, up from $483 million last year. The modernisation projects include the introduction of new Fiat models and part of a $100 million electricity and steam co-generation plant.

The group exceeded its 10 percent growth target in 1996 and increased its turnover by 13 percent to 975 trillion lira, or $12 billion dollars. It aims to raise the total turnover to between 1,900 and 2,000 trillion lira this year.
Turkey's annual inflation runs at around 80 percent.
Arikan said Koc's target was to be a Turkey-based international group concentrating on automotive, white goods and food industries as well as supermarket chains and finance.
But the group has expanded into other areas as well.
"We decided to enter energy and telecommunication sectors," Arikan said.

The group bid in the privatisation tenders of regional power distribution networks in partnership with U.S. based energy group NRG and UK based Pea Body. The consortium also plans to bid in tenders to operate thermal power plants, expected to be announced next month.
Arikan said they were also preparing to participate in the privatisation of Turk Telekom whose 10 percent stake is envisaged to be tendered for sell-off in late 1997.
